# Decision Owner memo — Worked Example: Estimate — Fermi Magnitude Rebuild (Thermal Energy Storage)

> **To:** Decision Owner\
> **Re:** Worked Example: Estimate — Fermi Magnitude Rebuild (Thermal Energy Storage)\
> **Basis:** analysis-20260101T000002Z.md\
> **Band (from §6):** MEDIUM

*Derived from §6 and the structured summary of analysis-20260101T000002Z.md; the six sections remain the source of truth.*

In brief: The analysis rebuilds the installed cost of molten-salt thermal storage from unit factors and tests it against lithium-ion storage on a like-for-like basis (§1, C1).

It examined whether a 5 MWh molten-salt store is cost-competitive with lithium-ion, which matters because a store-only price set against a whole-system price had earlier made molten-salt look cheaper (§1, §5 "Comparing the store's cost with the battery's installed price").

It has settled that the store itself is cheap, at $12.0–$34.4/kWh_th installed, and that pricing the power block is what decides the comparison (C1, GT-8).

Confidence is MEDIUM because GT-7? is carried rather than read at source, although the verdict no longer turns on it (§6, GT-7?).

This analysis has no Answer block; its recommendation and the conditions it depends on are stated in §6. That recommendation is conditioned on a four-hour discharge duration, and a power-block quotation at this system's scale could only move the break-even toward longer durations (§6, C1).
